title: Multivalent supramolecular fluorescent probes for accurate disease imaging

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction (paragraph on MPS mitigation strategies) vs. Abstract/Introduction conclusion on AKI diagnosis
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper explicitly argues that existing strategies which increase renal clearance rate are useful 'primarily to renal disease imaging' precisely because they shorten circulation half-life ('While this approach increases the renal clearance rate of the probes, it concurrently shortens their circulation half-life, thus restricting their use primarily to renal disease imaging'). The authors then state their own design goal is the opposite: 'a probe design that circumvents MPS capture without accelerating clearance, thereby extending the circulation time of the probe.' Yet the abstract and introduction claim this same long-circulating, non-renally-cleared probe design achieves 'substantial advancements in the early diagnosis of acute kidney injury.' This is a direct internal contradiction: the paper's own stated rationale implies that probes designed to avoid fast clearance (opposite of the renal-clearance strategy) should be less, not more, suited to renal injury diagnosis than the renal-clearance-promoting probes they criticize, yet no alternative mechanism is given in the available text to reconcile how prolonged circulation/MPS evasion specifically improves AKI detection better than the cited renal-clearance approaches.
